title: Security onboarding snapshot — SIEM payloads & RBAC v2 overview
content:
Purpose
This one-page snapshot is intended for customer security reviewers and internal onboarding owners. It summarizes: RBAC v2 primitives and mapping guidance; the audit-log schema we export; example SIEM payloads for common evidence requests; and a lightweight plan for automating questionnaire responses (evidence automation). Use this as a quick reference during security reviews and as the basis for trust-center copy and a customer-facing FAQ.

Status and scope
- Status: draft, internal review.
- Scope: hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments where telemetry and audit-log exports are available.
- Not included: detailed HSM/KMS key lifecycle (see separate key-management brief).

Quick RBAC v2 summary (customer-facing language)
- Roles vs. permissions: RBAC v2 defines a set of first-class roles (admin, security-admin, infra-operator, app-developer, read-only) plus fine-grained permission flags (invoke-model, manage-deployments, view-audit, export-logs).
- Tenancy model: role assignments are applied at the tenant (org) and project (workspace) layers. Cross-tenant delegation is disabled by default.
- Audit-focused roles: we expose a read-only audit role that can be scoped to time ranges and routes; customers can create service-accounts with only export and read-audit permissions for SIEM ingestion.
- Common guidance for questionnaires: provide tenant-scoped screenshots of the RBAC UI, list of default roles, and an exported CSV of role bindings for the requester’s org (redact user IDs as needed).

Audit-log schema (top-level fields we export)
We maintain a compact, SIEM-ready line-schema for all production activity. Minimal required fields:
- timestamp: ISO-8601 UTC
- tenant_id: opaque org identifier (UUID)
- principal_id: user or service account id (pseudonymized on request)
- principal_type: USER | SERVICE_ACCOUNT | SYSTEM
- event_type: string (e.g., auth_success, model_invoke, deployment_create, role_grant, audit_export)
- route: API route or console path (e.g., /v1/chat/completions)
- request_id: globally unique per request (for trace joins)
- outcome: SUCCESS | FAILURE | WARNING
- details: free-text summary or structured kv pairs (we try to limit to flat kvs for easier SIEM indexing)

Example SIEM payload (flattened JSON line for ingestion)
{
  "timestamp": "2024-11-04T15:22:09Z",
  "tenant_id": "org_9f3b2a7e",
  "principal_id": "svc_analytics_01",
  "principal_type": "SERVICE_ACCOUNT",
  "event_type": "audit_export",
  "route": "/admin/audit/export",
  "request_id": "req_3b1c9d2f",
  "outcome": "SUCCESS",
  "details": "exported 2024-11-01..2024-11-04 logs; filters:event_type=model_invoke"
}
Notes on PI/PHI and pseudonymization
- We default to pseudonymized principal_id in cross-customer exports.
- For tenant-local exports (customer requests), we can provide reversible pseudonyms if the customer has an approved data processing agreement and justification.

SIEM export variants we support
- Syslog/CEF: line-oriented export for SIEMs that prefer syslog.
- JSON over HTTPS (push): structured JSON lines to a customer-managed ingestion endpoint (mutual TLS supported).
- S3/Cloud Storage buckets: batch exports in NDJSON with nightly partitioning.
- Kafka: event stream for high-throughput customers.

Mapping guidance for common customer asks
- "Provide me an audit report for the last 90 days": deliver NDJSON export for requested window + a summary CSV with counts per event_type + a high-level integrity statement (hashes).
- "Show role binding evidence": provide RBAC export CSV (columns: binding_id, role, subject_type, subject_id, created_at, source) + screenshot of the UI that generated the export.
- "How do we ingest logs into our SIEM?": recommend JSON-over-HTTPS for near-real-time, S3 for compliance archives; provide a sample parsing map for common SIEM vendors (Splunk, QRadar, Sumo).

Evidence automation proposal (lightweight, 3-month MVP)
Goal: reduce manual effort when answering common security questionnaire items by auto-assembling evidence bundles.
- Inputs: question key (from standard questionnaire libraries), customer org id, time window, artifact selectors (logs, role exports, policy snapshots).
- Engine: map question key to one or more extractors (e.g., extract_rbac_bindings, extract_audit_slice, export_siem_sample). Extractors produce flat artifacts (CSV, NDJSON, PDF screenshot).
- Delivery: signed ZIP with manifest.json (manifest is small plaintext mapping names to included files and SHA256 hashes), optionally uploaded to customer S3.
- Controls: evidence bundles are generated only when a request is authorized by a security-admin role; generation requests are logged and rate-limited.
- Low-risk MVP: focus on the top 20 questionnaire items we see in the field (RBAC, audit retention, export tooling, encryption at rest).

Operational controls and integrity guarantees
- Tamper-evidence: every batch export includes a signed manifest and an export-level signature (HMAC) tied to an export key retained under CMK.
- Retention and purging: audit logs default retention 90 days for Hosted; Dedicated/private can configure retention to customer policy.
- Access controls: only service accounts with export_logs permission can call the export API; UI exports require two-step confirmation for org-level exports.

Customer FAQ snippets (short answers for questionnaire boxes)
- Q: Can we get role binding exports? A: Yes — we can export RBAC bindings as CSV scoped to your org and time window. Please request via the Security Access request flow.
- Q: What does the audit log include? A: Timestamps, tenant/principal identifiers, request route, request id, outcome, and minimal details. We can provide additional fields on a case-by-case basis.
- Q: How do you prevent data exfiltration during export? A: Exports are controlled by RBAC, signed manifests, and optional upload to customer-owned buckets. All export activity is logged and subject to review.

Next steps (internal)
- Review draft with SOC and Product (target meeting: 2024-12-12).
- Prepare two artifacts for trust-center: a short customer-facing one-pager and a technical appendix with SIEM parsing examples for Splunk and QRadar.
- Prototype extractor for RBAC bindings and audit slice (sprint 1).

Open questions / decisions needed
- Decide default pseudonymization policy for tenant-local exports (reversible vs irreversible).
- Finalize signed-manifest format (self-contained vs separate signature service).

Appendix: short checklist for security reviewers
- [ ] Confirm requested time window and tenant scope.
- [ ] Verify requestor identity and RBAC permission.
- [ ] Choose export channel (HTTPS / S3 / Syslog) and confirm endpoint.
- [ ] Generate bundle -> verify manifest hashes -> deliver to customer.

Owner and contact
Aisha Banerjee (product-security) — aisha@redwood.ai

End of snapshot
